It also leaves out context an investigator would need.","problems":["The rationale says \"Charts support billing\" and also \"Too few 99215 charts to resolve the claims outlier\". With only 4 documented 99215 charts, the first statement overreaches and conflicts with the second and with the inconclusive leaning.","Both cited example claims are low-complexity 99215s (0 and 1 conditions), and neither has a returned chart. The documented 99215 examples (C0050480, C0050541, C0051057, C0051181) are not mentioned. Nothing separates which cited visits have documentation and which don't. C0051181 is documented and also low-complexity (0 conditions, Z09), which makes it the most informative claim to cite, but it is not cited.","The 'wrong-content first response' in the headline is accurate. But it omits the deficiencies in round 2 (ILLEGIBLE, MISSING_RESULTS), which affect how reliable the 29 charts are.","The summary doesn't explain the gap between the 2.97 ratio to expected and the plain z of 0.92. It also doesn't use the complexity gradient, such as 44.8% of 99215 visits in the 5+ condition group against 3.1% in the 0 group. That gradient would show whether the billing tracks patient complexity.","Next steps are generic. The next step asks for a targeted 99215 sample but does not state sample size, and it does not mention the 2 notes with data claimed but no lab line.","The 7% comparison rate for 99215 below-billed is stated without clarification that it is a comparison figure from the card (all_provider_rate 0.067), which is fine but thin."]}
